Name: Cozy Desert Farm Redux plus Desert Crops
Author: HarrisonGrey
Description:
[center]Want a unique farming experience in Stardew Valley? Played the old version of the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/9184]Cozy Desert Farm[/url]﻿ and want a more fleshed out version? Look no further than the [b]Cozy Desert Farm Redux! [/b]Selectable from the menu as an additional farm type, this is a remake of my previous mod with some major upgrades.[/center]

[b]Farming in the Desert[/b]
﻿The Cozy Desert Farm is a smaller plot of land in a harsh environment, where sprinklers won't work on the hot desert sand. Cliffs box you in, and water is scarce, with a small river on the far side of the farm and a barrel near your farmhouse. There are no trees except for a couple palm trees by the river. But as you progress you'll unlock more areas, which include some unique advantages. All the sand and grass tiles are diggable and buildable.
﻿Clearing debris will eventually unlock two small grottos and a plateau, all with soil that does allow for sprinklers. A locked door can eventually be opened, giving you access to a small cavern that allows both out of season crops [i]and[/i] casks.
﻿The river on the main farm has access to town fish and desert fish like the Sandfish; after you've reached the Calico Desert, you'll be able to catch the Scorpion Carp back on the farm as well. The grottos also have their own cave ponds, complete with cave fish like the Ghostfish and Stonefish.
﻿On the other side of the river there is a conspicuously indented section of cliff face; while your tools won't do anything to it, once you've unlocked the Calico Desert the wall will crumble on its own, granting you a shortcut to the Desert. The shortcut works even during the Desert Festival.

[b]Succulent Crops[/b]
﻿What kind of desert farmer doesn't cultivate cacti and succulents? To take advantage of the desert environment, there are three new crops that combine with the vanilla Cactus Fruit to form a succulent quartet. All four crops can be planted in the ground on the desert farm as well as in the Calico Desert, grow in all four seasons, and do not need watering. In addition to the edits to the Cactus Fruit, the new crops are:
﻿[b]Moss Rose[/b]: a fast growing, weedy succulent, this plant can be propagated simply by planting cuttings. Not purchasable, you'll find cuttings while foraging through the Valley in Spring and Summer; plant the cuttings back home and you'll get more back than you planted. Similar to the Coffee Bean, this crop has no seed item, and its own produce can be planted to grow more. The plant is also a cooking ingredient; while the cuttings aren't edible on their own, they can be pickled in the Preserves Jar, dried in the Dehydrator, or cooked with Vinegar into a new recipe, Portulaca Salad.
﻿[b]Cactus Flower[/b]: A paddle shaped cactus that grows beautiful light purple flowers. You can find cuttings for this crop at the Desert Trader, and once planted it keeps producing even after its first harvest.
﻿The mysterious [b]Calico Sprout[/b]: dig around in the Calico Desert long enough, and you may unearth a green cutting from some kind of succulent plant. This can only be planted in the Calico Desert or on the Cozy Desert Farm, and it will take a [i]long[/i] time to grow. But keep at it, and you may grow something quite valuable. Calico Sprouts can be dug up from artifact spots in the Calico Desert or on the Desert Farm, purchased from the Egg Trader at the Desert Festival, or dropped by Giant Crops.
﻿[b]Giant Crops[/b]: All four of the Desert Crops, when planted in a 3x3 grid, have a rare chance to form the [b]Giant Cactus Garden[/b], a Giant Crop that, when chopped down, grants not only extra produce of the crop that made it, but a small amount of the others as well, including rare Calico Sprouts. The Giant Crop can only be formed by 9 [i]of the same crop[/i], though all four will make the same Giant Crop. The Giant Crop has an alternate blooming form in the more temperate seasons of Spring and Fall.
﻿Each of the three new crops (and the edits made to the Cactus Fruit) can be toggled separately in the Config menu; each one can separately be disabled, enabled only on the Cozy Desert Farm, or enabled across all saves.

[b]Config Options[/b]
﻿This farm is highly configurable; in addition to the configurable Desert Crops, you can also change:

﻿"[i]Starter Gift[/i]": What gift do you receive at the beginning of the game. Your options are [b]Desert Farmer[/b] (9 Parsnips and 6 Moss Rose Cuttings); [b]Beekeeper[/b] (2 Bee Houses and 10 Tulips); [b]Arborist[/b] (1 Orange Sapling and 3 Tappers); or [b]Barista[/b] (10 Tea Leaves and 1 Keg). The Getting Started quest also changes depending on which Starter Gift you choose. Default is Desert Farmer; [i]remember, you must make your selection before starting your farm[/i].
﻿"[i]Desert Shortcut[/i]": The shortcut to the Calico Desert can be disabled if it would cause interference with mods that make edits to the Desert map. SVE, for instance, changes the desert dramatically and the shortcut will be automatically disabled if you have SVE installed. [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/31595]Desert Expansion[/url], on the other hand, is wholly compatible.
﻿"[i]Recolor Selection[/i]": This mod uses a custom tilesheet which you can configure to match other recolor mods. Currently supported recolors are DaisyNiko's Earthy Recolor, Yri's Retro Recolor, and Starblue Valley.
﻿"[i]Desert Sprinklers[/i]": I know someone will want this, so sprinklers can be enabled on the desert sand. I like the challenge, but if we wanted a purely curated experience we wouldn't be on a modding website. Disabled by default.
﻿"[i]Desert Dirt[/i]": This map uses a custom texture for the tilled dirt while on the Desert Farm (and in the Desert); you can disable this, just in case it interferes with other recolor mods.

[b]Compatibilities[/b]
﻿[b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/3753]SVE[/url][/b]: With the Desert Shortcut disabled, this mod should be fully compatible.
﻿[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/31595]Desert Expansion[/url]: Fully compatible, even with the shortcut enabled.
﻿[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/40844]Sandy Sprinklers[/url], and similar mods: This mod uses its own custom tilesheet to disable sprinklers on the desert sand, as a result mods that enable sprinklers on sand don't affect this one. If you want to enable sprinklers on the farm's desert sand, you can change that in the config menu.
﻿[b]Farm Cave mods[/b]: this mod does not affect the Farm Cave, so mods that change the Farm Cave map should work just fine.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5255]﻿DaisyNiko's Earthy Recolor[/url]: Compatible; the custom tilesheet for this mod does not change automatically, but you can manually change it in the config menu to match.
﻿[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/36292]Yri's Retro Recolor[/url]: Custom tilesheet for compatibility.
﻿[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/21085]Starblue Valley[/url]: Custom tilesheet for compatibility.

[b]Translate Me![/b]
﻿This mod is i18n ready and can be translated; feel free to post translations yourself or send them to me and I can add them in an update. Please don't use ai to translate this.
Chinese translation by 180nw.
